nodes.bron.text.t: "Weapons? A pitchfork'll do you. If you want something better, try the trader at the stalls, but he buys from thieves and his prices are thieving too."

nodes.interes.text.t: "I shoe horses for imperial messengers, who pay in chits, and for peasants, who pay in eggs. At least you can eat eggs. A chit you can burn at best, and it makes a poor fire at that."

nodes.kopalnia_plotka.text.t: "It didn't fall from the sky. It comes from a merchant's storehouse, like every smith's in the Empire." Bogdan rubs his beard. "Though once I bought a bar off a man from the Old Mine, four days down the trail. The metal there is different, cold in the hand. Not everyone can stand it. It sings to me at night."

nodes.kuznia.options.[papiery_po].text.t: How are my papers coming along?

nodes.kuznia.options.[q4_kg].text.t: The wise woman says someone visits you at night with a wineskin.

nodes.kuznia.options.[q5_koniec].text.t: I was up on the hill. I saw red cloaks.

nodes.kuznia.options.[q5_start].text.t: What are you afraid of round here?

nodes.kuznia.options.[technologia].text.t: I know the stones from the sky. I know what they can do.

nodes.kuznia.text.t: Bogdan the smith is hammering at a piece of iron. "Horseshoes, scythes, hooks, nails. I don't forge swords, the Emperor keeps those for himself and guards them better than his own wives. What do you want?"

nodes.papiery_po.text.t: "At first glance they're imperial, and at second glance more or less. Don't show them to anyone who's read more than five pages. And if someone asks whose papers they are, say your cousin's. Everybody's got some cousin."

nodes.q4_kg.text.t: Bogdan stops hammering, which for him is about as rare as confession. "The pilgrim. He wanders in, drinks, asks about the guests at the tavern and who's come over the pass. He buys nails and pays in coin with the imperial eagle on it. Tell the reeve it's the one from the road, and that I'm not afraid, just careful."

nodes.q5_koniec.text.t: Bogdan listens stone-faced and only swallows at the very end. "Red cloaks, a campfire and the watch changed every two hours. Means they're staying. Better to know early than too late. And the graveyard's been getting interesting of a night too, but that's none of my business. Here's ten groats and some advice: don't go that way in what you've got on your back."

nodes.q5_start.text.t: Bogdan wipes his paws on his leather apron and lowers his voice. "Someone's keeping a fire going on the hill beyond the shrine. Not a shepherd, a shepherd's got no reason to. Go up there, have a look round, come back and tell me what you saw. If it's Imperials, I want to know how many. If not, I want to know who, 'cause I'd rather have neighbours I know."

nodes.q6_kuj.text.t: Bogdan sniffs the wax, nods and puts it away in a box. "Papers? I'll make them. A smith with an imperial seal is a nasty mix, but who said I have to live safe? Give me a moment, it'll look just like the real thing. Almost. Nobody checks if they're genuine, they just watch your face." A while later he lays a scrap of paper in front of you that smells of smoke and swindle.

nodes.technologia.text.t: Bogdan puts down his hammer and gives you a long look. "You know, do you? Then don't brag about it in front of people. In Głuszec a stone from the sky is no wonder, it's a death sentence. If you ever want to talk it over quietly, you know where the forge is."
